task:
Perform a Kubernetes cluster upgrade using kubeadm.

Steps (adjust version numbers to what's available on your cluster):

  1. Check current version and available upgrades:
     kubeadm upgrade plan

  2. On the control plane node:
     a. Upgrade kubeadm:  apt-mark unhold kubeadm && apt install kubeadm=1.XX.X-* && apt-mark hold kubeadm
     b. Verify plan:      kubeadm upgrade plan
     c. Apply upgrade:    kubeadm upgrade apply v1.XX.X
     d. Upgrade kubelet:  apt-mark unhold kubelet kubectl && apt install kubelet=1.XX.X-* kubectl=1.XX.X-* && apt-mark hold kubelet kubectl
     e. Restart:          systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet

  3. On each worker node (SSH in, then):
     a. Drain from control plane: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets
     b. Upgrade kubeadm + apply node upgrade: kubeadm upgrade node
     c. Upgrade kubelet, restart
     d. Uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>

  4. Verify all nodes show the new version: kubectl get nodes
hints: kubeadm upgrade plan shows available versions
Always upgrade control plane first, then workers
Drain each worker before upgrading it
detailed_hints: Use 'apt-cache madison kubeadm' to see available versions
Hold packages after upgrade to prevent unintentional upgrades: apt-mark hold kubeadm kubelet kubectl
Check node versions after: kubectl get nodes -o wide

validators.command: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l component=kube-apiserver -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.phase}'
